pharm: Inhibits fungal cytochrome P450-dependent 14-alpha-demethylase, blocking ergosterol synthesis in the fungal cell membrane.
quick: 200 mg once daily (blastomycosis/histoplasmosis); up to 400 mg/day
Take capsules with a full meal
Avoid; teratogenic in animals (not for onychomycosis)
Use caution; do not use IV if CrCl <30 (cyclodextrin vehicle)
Use with caution; monitor LFTs; boxed risk of hepatotoxicity
LFTs, signs of CHF, cardiac/respiratory symptoms
summary: Itraconazole is an oral triazole antifungal for systemic fungal infections including blastomycosis, histoplasmosis, and aspergillosis, plus onychomycosis. It is a potent CYP3A4 inhibitor with numerous contraindicated drug interactions and carries a boxed warning for congestive heart failure and drug interactions.
indications: Histoplasmosis (including chronic cavitary pulmonary and disseminated non-meningeal)
Pulmonary and extrapulmonary aspergillosis in patients intolerant of or refractory to amphotericin B
Onychomycosis of toenail (with or without fingernail involvement) due to dermatophytes
Onychomycosis of fingernail due to dermatophytes

dosage.d: 200 mg once daily; increase by 100 mg increments to max 400 mg/day (doses >200 mg/day in 2 divided doses)
dosage.n: Take with a full meal; swallow capsules whole

dosage.d: Loading dose 200 mg three times daily (600 mg/day) for first 3 days

admin: Confirm diagnosis with appropriate cultures/specimens before therapy
Take capsules with a full meal to maximize absorption
Do NOT interchange capsules with oral solution (different bioavailability)
Review all concomitant medications for CYP3A4 interactions before starting
moa: Itraconazole inhibits fungal cytochrome P450 14-alpha-demethylase, the enzyme converting lanosterol to ergosterol. Depletion of ergosterol disrupts the fungal cell membrane, halting fungal growth.

absolute: Coadministration with CYP3A4 substrates that prolong QT or cause serious toxicity (e.g., methadone, disopyramide, dofetilide, dronedarone, quinidine, isavuconazole, ergot alkaloids, lovastatin/simvastatin, oral midazolam, triazolam, cisapride, pimozide, certain others)
Treatment of onychomycosis in patients with ventricular dysfunction (CHF or history of CHF)
relative: Hepatic impairment or elevated liver enzymes

preg: Avoid in pregnancy; itraconazole caused dose-related maternal toxicity, embryotoxicity, and teratogenicity (skeletal defects in rats, encephalocele/macroglossia in mice). No adequate human studies. Contraindicated for onychomycosis in pregnancy and in women contemplating pregnancy.
lact: Itraconazole is excreted in human milk; weigh expected maternal benefit against potential infant exposure. CDC advises HIV-infected women not to breastfeed.
renal: Use with caution. Itraconazole pharmacokinetics not significantly altered in mild-moderate renal impairment; IV formulation (hydroxypropyl-beta-cyclodextrin vehicle) should not be used if CrCl <30 mL/min.
hepatic: Use with caution; hepatotoxicity (including rare fatal liver failure) reported. Monitor LFTs, especially in pre-existing hepatic disease or with prolonged therapy.

major: CYP3A4 substrates with narrow therapeutic index: methadone, disopyramide, dofetilide, dronedarone, quinidine, ergot alkaloids, lovastatin, simvastatin, oral midazolam, triazolam, cisapride, pimozide (contraindicated)
Calcium channel blockers (additive negative inotropy; risk of CHF)
Drugs that reduce gastric acid or CYP3A4 inducers (rifampin, phenytoin, carbamazepine) reduce itraconazole levels
interactions.food: Capsules require a full meal for absorption; gastric acidity needed for capsule absorption.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid due to additive hepatotoxicity risk.

emergency: Signs of heart failure (dyspnea, edema, weight gain)

monitoring: Liver function tests at baseline and periodically
counsel: Take capsules with a full meal
Report shortness of breath, leg swelling, or unusual fatigue immediately
Report jaundice, dark urine, severe abdominal pain, or appetite loss
Do not start new medications without checking for interactions
Complete the full course of therapy
pk: Antifungal effect over days to weeks
16-28 hr single dose; 34-42 hr with repeated dosing
Accumulates in tissues (nails, skin) for weeks
Store at controlled room temperature 15-25 C (59-77 F)
pearls: Capsules need gastric acid and food; PPIs/H2 blockers reduce absorption
Capsule and oral solution are NOT interchangeable
Potent CYP3A4 inhibitor; always screen interaction list
Boxed warning: do not use for onychomycosis in patients with CHF or history of CHF
missed: Take as soon as remembered with food; if near the next dose, skip the missed dose. Do not double up.
overdose: No specific antidote. Itraconazole is not removed by dialysis. Provide supportive care; gastric lavage and activated charcoal may be considered if recent ingestion.
